summary: Up 0.1 on w13 (8.3), still just below 8.5, with no high-severity issues. Fixed or improved: (1) The trim-A ears now have their own tile with chunky chips (render chip size p50 17 px vs 10 in w13, aspect 1.38, chip/ground 1.82 vs py_37305 1.88), so the sliver regression is gone. (2) The back weave now sits in ordered brick rows, so the 'TV static' read is gone (w14a_back.png). (3) The pocket is 7.5 cm lower (recess bottom 0.345 -> 0.27), with a rear holder plate and a wide centred leaflet. (4) The cushion saturation is close to the photo (S 0.16 vs 0.18). Still wrong: (a) The ear chips render as convex, regular hexagons with smooth edges, which reads as polka dots (q13b foreground, p4, q14 right edge). py_37305 shows ragged, notched petals with frosty fringes, a wide size spread (several big chips about 2x the median area) and many tiny specks. The notch is not visible in the tile, and the 140 specks are too faint to see. The ear ground is still too blue (S 0.26-0.29 vs 0.15-0.17). (b) The w13 'flatter, steadier' change overshot the back contrast: p8 float cover 19.4 % vs 14.6 % in py_37301, high-pass 0.219 vs 0.188, p90/p50 1.39 vs 1.30, S 0.26 vs 0.21. (c) About 0.11-0.15 m of plain shell plus the silver line is still left between the pocket and the footrest. b_san_20 / san_26 show 2-5 cm. (d) Close up (p5), the cushion is an 8-bit pixel mosaic of square-edged blocks. py_37301's cushion is fine, ribbed dash rows. (e) Small items are unchanged: the navy flap is flat, the placards are blank, and the holder plate is a plain rectangle.
lighting_note: Not scored. In q13 the whole PY block reads cobalt-blue and the navy flaps read royal blue, against the neutral grey seats and dark-navy flaps in py_37302. Studio p8 S is 0.26 against 0.21, so roughly half of this is material and half is exposure / tone mapping. q14 has a bright rhombus-shaped sun or specular patch on the far window seat back (around x 500, y 330). Check whether that is the window sun LUT.

issues.fix: test/make_swatches.py synth_py_confetti(ear=True): (1) Make the notch survive. Apply it after the polygon as a cut, prof *= 1 - 0.45 * exp(-((abs(th) - pi) / 0.35)**2), on about 60 % of the chips. Add a second, smaller notch at th = pi +- 0.9 on about 30 %, giving a 2-3 lobe petal edge. (2) Make the edges ragged: prof *= 1 + 0.12 * blurred noise sampled per pixel (_blur_wrap(rng.normal(0, 1, (S, S)), 1.0) normalised), and dither a 1-2 px frosty fringe of 0.5-gain pixels outside prof. (3) Widen the size spread: req = exp(normal(log 8, 0.45)), clipped 4-17, with 22 chips at min spacing 24 px, so a few are big. (4) Make the specks visible: 90 specks of radius 1-2 px at gain 1.5-2.5 instead of 140 at 0.3-0.6 with radius 2-5. Keep the chip gain at 4.2. Target in p4: cover 16-18 %, blob p90 at least 45 px, at least 60 blobs under 8 px.
